dedupe_keys.name: finap finnish national access point for mobility services and traffic data

description: FINAP is Finland's national access point under EU rules, gathering Finnish transport datasets in one place. The page says road authorities and service providers must supply data on road infrastructure, road traffic, mobility services and alternative fuel distribution networks, so that traffic data can be shared and reused in digital services such as navigation. Finland currently has two access points: a mobility services catalogue, where operators provide descriptions, routes, timetables, prices and booking and sales interfaces, and a traffic data catalogue for road and street infrastructure, rules and restrictions, network use and status and fuel networks. Under legislation in force from 1 January 2026, operation is being centralised in Fintraffic and the two points merge during 2026. Coverage: Finland. Format and access: public catalogues. Licence and cost: free to browse; terms per dataset. Caveats: the structure is changing during 2026. It supports network flow and emergency response studies. It relates to Digitraffic, the EU list of national access points and DATEX II in the catalogue.
